title: Things to Do in Havelock Island (Swaraj Dweep): Beaches, Diving & Sunsets
seoTitle: Things to Do in Havelock Island (Swaraj Dweep) | Kudozz Club
description: Things to do in Havelock Island: sunset at Radhanagar, snorkelling and sea walks at Elephant beach, scuba diving courses and fun dives, Kalapathar and Vijaynagar beaches, night kayaking for bioluminescence, forest walks and island cafés.
dek: The best-known island in the Andamans, with a long white beach famous for its sunsets, clear water over coral reefs and a relaxed dive-town feel.
primaryKeyword: things to do in Havelock Island
searchIntent: Honeymooners, families and divers planning two to four nights on Havelock and deciding what to book.

hero.caption: Radhanagar beach

intro: Havelock Island, officially renamed Swaraj Dweep in 2018, lies about two hours by ferry north-east of Port Blair. It is the most visited island in the Andamans, with a few villages, a string of beaches on its eastern and western coasts and dense tropical forest in between.

The things to do on Havelock are mostly about the sea: long afternoons and sunsets at Radhanagar, snorkelling and water sports at Elephant beach, scuba diving with dozens of dive schools, quieter beaches such as Kalapathar and Vijaynagar, and, on dark nights, kayaking through mangroves lit by bioluminescence.
Two to four nights is ideal. October to May is the best season; November to April is best for diving.

items.name: Watch sunset at Radhanagar
body: Radhanagar beach, on the west coast, is a long crescent of white sand backed by tall trees. The water is calm and clear for much of the season, and the sunset draws everyone on the island. Lifeguards are on duty during the day; heed flags and avoid swimming after dark.

The beach gets crowded in the late afternoon in peak season. For quieter moments, go in the morning, or walk towards the northern end where a small path leads to Neil's Cove, a sheltered corner with clear water.

items.name: Snorkel at Elephant beach
body: Elephant beach, reached by boat from the jetty or by a trek of about 2 km through forest, has shallow coral close to shore. Snorkelling, sea walking, glass-bottom boats and jet skis are offered.

items.name: Watch sunrise at Kalapathar
body: Kalapathar, on the east coast, is a quiet beach with black rocks, turquoise water and a road running alongside. It is the best spot on the island for sunrise.

items.name: Relax on Vijaynagar beach
body: Vijaynagar (Beach No. 5), on the east coast, is lined with resorts and mahua trees. At low tide the sea retreats far out, and it is a peaceful place for walks.

items.name: Do a try dive
body: Many dive schools offer a try dive (discover scuba) for non-divers, with a short briefing and a shallow dive with an instructor. No swimming ability is strictly required at some schools, but you should be comfortable in water. Choose a reputable operator affiliated with an international agency.

items.name: Get certified or fun dive
body: Havelock is one of the best places in India to learn to dive, with courses of three to four days. Certified divers can explore sites such as the Wall, Dixon's Pinnacle, Aquarium and Johnny's Gorge, with coral, reef fish, turtles, rays and sometimes sharks.

items.name: Kayak for bioluminescence
body: Guided night kayaking trips through the mangrove creeks on dark nights, around the new moon, reveal bioluminescent plankton glowing with every paddle stroke. Daytime mangrove kayaking is also offered.

items.name: Try game fishing or a snorkelling boat trip
body: Boat trips go to snorkelling spots around the island, and some operators offer game fishing trips further out. Check licences and safety equipment.

items.name: Walk the forest trail
body: The trail from the main road to Elephant beach passes through forest with huge trees and birdsong. It can be muddy after rain; go with a guide and wear good shoes.

items.name: Eat at cafés and seafood shacks
body: Havelock's villages along the main road have cafés, bakeries and seafood restaurants, many run by settlers from Bengal and elsewhere. Try grilled fish, crab and Bengali fish curry.

items.name: Take a day trip to Neil Island
body: Neil (Shaheed Dweep) is about an hour away by ferry, with a natural rock bridge and quiet beaches. Many travellers stay a night there after Havelock.

items.name: October to December
body: Seas calm after the monsoon, the island is green and diving season begins. December is busy and expensive.

items.name: January to April
body: The best time for diving and snorkelling, with clear water and calm seas.

items.name: May to September
body: Monsoon rain and rough seas; ferries are sometimes cancelled and many dive schools slow down or close.

byTraveller.text: Sunset at Radhanagar, a try dive, night kayaking and a quiet resort on Vijaynagar.
Elephant beach snorkelling and glass-bottom boats, and calm afternoons at Radhanagar.
Four to five days for a certification course and fun dives.

oneDay: Watch sunrise at Kalapathar, then take a boat to Elephant beach for snorkelling. After lunch, spend the afternoon at Radhanagar and stay for sunset. On a dark night, join a bioluminescence kayak trip.
tips: Government and private ferries run from Port Blair; book early in peak season.
ATMs on the island can run out of cash; carry some.
Mobile data is slow; download maps offline.
Do not touch or stand on coral when snorkelling.

faqs.q: What are the best things to do on Havelock Island?
faqs.a: Watch sunset at Radhanagar, snorkel at Elephant beach, scuba dive, see sunrise at Kalapathar, relax at Vijaynagar and kayak for bioluminescence.

faqs.q: Can non-swimmers scuba dive on Havelock?
faqs.a: Many schools offer try dives for non-swimmers with close instructor support, but being comfortable in water is important. Check with the operator.

faqs.q: How many days are enough for Havelock?
Is Havelock now called Swaraj Dweep?
faqs.a: Yes. It was renamed Swaraj Dweep in 2018, though Havelock is still widely used.

faqs.q: When is bioluminescence visible on Havelock?
faqs.a: On dark nights around the new moon, especially in the dry season. Guided kayak trips through the mangroves offer the best chance.
